# Harsh Pratap Singh

> Personal blog about Engineering, Research, and building things.

## About

Harsh Pratap Singh is a competent software engineer and researcher focused on Distributed Systems, Machine Learning, Databases, and Cryptography. This site contains technical writeups, reading lists, and a resume.

## Site Structure

- https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/ - Home page with bio and links
- https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/ - Technical blog posts about engineering and research
- https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/reads/ - Curated reading lists for CS, Philosophy, Startups, and Finance
- https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/resume/ - Professional experience and work history

## Writes

- [Living the GitHub Actions Dream](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/living-the-github-actions-dream/): Making Docker builds and GitHub Actions CI fast with BuildKit, caching, Arm runners, and Rust build tips
- [All sorts of famous Attention Layers](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/all-sorts-of-famous-attention-layers/): A tour of attention variants from classic softmax attention through modern efficient designs
- [missing writing some concurrency in Go](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/missing-writing-go/): Go concurrency patterns from production, channels, CSP, and synchronization beyond the happy path
- [i should have paid a closer look at tokenizer](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/i-should-have-paid-a-closer-look-at-tokenizer/): What tokenizers do, how BPE training works, and why token boundaries matter for cost and behavior
- [cutting that inference cost](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/cutting-that-inference-cost/): Practical notes on LLM inference cost and latency with vLLM, SGLang, PagedAttention, and KV cache
- [some insights on HNSW](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/some-insights-on-hnsw/): How HNSW approximate nearest neighbor search works for RAG and the recall versus latency tradeoff
- [how package managers use PubGrub for Dependency Resolution](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/pubgrub-for-dependency-resolution/): PubGrub dependency resolution in package managers like uv, CDCL, conflicts, and backtracking
- [the longer you chat, the worse your agent's response](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/the-longer-you-chat-the-worse-your-agents-response/): Why long agent chats degrade, context collapse, memory layers, compaction, and evals
- [DB Joins on GPUs!!](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/db-joins-on-gpus/): Why SQL joins run fast on GPUs via hash joins, radix partitioning, and massive parallelism
- [Which Prompts Actually Work for your Agents?](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/which-prompts-actually-work-for-your-agents/): Prompt saliency analysis to find which system-prompt phrases actually drive agent behavior
- [The chronicles of training FBPINNs](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/the-chronicles-of-training-fbpinns/): Training FBPINNs on a supercomputer, GPU quirks, and distributed training resource constraints
- [The Rusty path to Secure Metrics in Ambient Mesh](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/istio-lfx/): Secure metrics for Istio Ambient Mesh ztunnel in Rust from an LFX internship
- [Do I officially qualify as a Software Engineer now?](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/do-i-officially-qualify-as-a-software-engineer/): Reflections after systems programming internships and writing Rust applications
- [The frenzy of building and observing seniors!](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/building/): Why rebuilding systems from scratch helps debugging and owning product technology
- [Working at a early-stage startup!](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/working-at-a-early-stage-startup/): Early-stage startup work versus internships: ownership, communication, and unblocking people
- [Starting to pick up Nix a bit!](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/nix/): A headstarter on Nix for reproducible systems, flakes, Nixpacks, and getting started resources
- [Spent my summers exploring Bitcoin](https://harsh-ps-2003.github.io/writes/sob/): Summer of Bitcoin 2024 notes on Fedimint, escrow modules, and learning Bitcoin by verifying the tech
